post.caption: This small brooch carries 76 patterns. The ring is under 9 centimeters across and its pin is over 30 centimeters long. A count in 1851 also found at least 76 patterns. Experts date it to around the eighth century, and studs of amber and glass sit among the patterns. It was reportedly found near Bettystown in 1850. Its name points to Tara, though it was not found there. Waterhouse showed it with smaller copies in London in 1851. By 1872 the Royal Irish Academy owned it. Today it is kept at the National Museum of Ireland in Dublin.
